Very poor experience, expensive and not tasty, the waiter's qualifications are average, but the environment is okay.
Sep 2026 • Friends
I am sharing my real experience, hoping it can be a reference for other customers. This restaurant charges a 13.4% tax. For example, if you choose a dish priced at 1.3 million VND, the final actual payment required is 1.47 million VND.
 
We arrived at the restaurant at six in the evening, which was just when the restaurant started operating. We wanted to order the five-dish set meal for 1.3 million VND, but the waiter informed us on the spot that two dishes in the set meal could not be provided. We were very surprised that there were sold-out dishes right after opening; it's hard to believe a restaurant with sufficient stock would have this situation. We are still willing to give the restaurant a chance and followed the waiter's suggestion to order à la carte, and the other party verbally promised that the total price would not be much more expensive than the set menu. But when checking out, I found that the actual base price was 60,000 VND higher than the original package. Although the difference is not huge, this concerns the reputation of the store. If the verbal explanation given by the waiter cannot be fulfilled, it is difficult for the customer to trust other information provided by the store.
 
Furthermore, the same waiter told us that the extra tax would not exceed 8%, but the final bill's tax rate was 13.4%, which is a very high rate I have seen while traveling in Vietnam and other places.
 
The dishes themselves aren't bad, but the overall experience completely fails to meet the standard for over 400 RMB.
 
The restaurant environment is acceptable, but only the environment is worth mentioning. The first attendant who received us was rather impatient. When we asked how to replace dishes in the package when some were missing, he lightly explained that this was for the customer's benefit. But the reality is that we not only spent more money but also didn't get the dishes we originally wanted, and the whole incident fully demonstrated the arrogance of the restaurant's handling of the problem. Fortunately, the gentleman who took over the service was friendly, which is commendable.
 
Overall, I don't think the store has the subjective intention of deliberately deceiving customers, but the store does need to improve the service staff's professional skills and emergency handling capabilities, while also improving kitchen ingredient preparation and strengthening information synchronization between the kitchen and the front desk.

Although the environment is good, there is a lack of integrity, the preparation is amateurish, and the cost-performance ratio is extremely low.
Sep 2026 • Friends
Arrived at the restaurant at 6 PM right when it opened for dinner, and the overall experience was disappointing. The core issues are misleading information and chaotic management:

Charges do not match verbal promises: The waiter clearly stated when taking the order that taxes would not exceed 8%, but the final bill was charged with taxes and service fees of up to 13.4% (a consumption of 1300k VND ended up costing over 1470k VND). Furthermore, because the set menu was missing dishes, and I followed the waiter's advice that "the à la carte price is almost the same as the set menu," the final à la carte amount was still 60k VND more than the set menu. Although the amount was small, the service staff's rambling directly damaged the restaurant's basic credibility.

Kitchen prep seriously negligent: At the beginning of the evening service, two dishes in the five-course set menu priced at 1300k VND were reported as sold out. A 40% shortage of dishes appeared at the time of opening to welcome guests, indicating significant flaws in the kitchen's ingredient planning and communication mechanism with the front of house.

Front lobby inducement for single points and false promotion: The attitude of the first receptionist was arrogant and impatient. When asked how to substitute missing dishes, the other party refused to make reasonable adjustments to the set menu, instead forcefully pushing for a complete switch to à la carte, while grandly claiming that "à la carte is more convenient for customers." In reality, they were shifting the restaurant's own preparation errors onto the consumer to save the kitchen and front-of-house staff trouble. What was worse was that during the negotiation, the waiter even blurted out that "the portion size of the dishes in the set menu is originally less than ordering individually," trying to use this tactic to induce us to give up the set menu. This behavior of belittling one's own package specifications and promoting higher consumption by fabricating differences in portion sizes is extremely unprofessional. Although the male waiter in the subsequent service was polite, it could not salvage the poor dining experience from before.

The dish flavors are mediocre and completely do not match the per-person price of nearly 400 RMB; apart from the decent decoration and environment, the overall experience was below expectations. If the restaurant does not seriously train front desk staff and standardize transparent pricing, it is not recommended to go.

reviews.review_text:

Singapore, Singapore534 contributions

Almost a Disaster, Otherwise Pleasant
Aug 2024 • Business
My department had a lunch at this restaurant while on our overseas trip to Vietnam. There were 32 persons in total. The food was good and serving portions were generous. The restaurant serves only a few vegetarian dishes and does not prepare Halal dishes. However, the restaurant permits catering of outside food for special dietary needs. The restaurant is spacious and able to accommodate many patrons. It is set in rustic ambience and even has a pond in the middle. While we were there, it was decorated with lanterns for the Mooncake festival. The reason for a low score is due to the ruining of the entire experience when it comes to payment. They were aware that we are foreigners but refused to accept payment by credit card. They only accept cash or bank transfer. When we attempted to make a bank transfer, a female staff presented a local bank QR code for us to scan to make the transfer. And because none of them are able to speak English, it took some effort to make her understand that the QR code doesn’t work for foreign banks. The female staff got impatient and showed her frustrations while I was setting up the details necessary for the bank transfer. She even tried to take my phone so that she is able to enter the details. I had to stop her because it is classified information. My personal bank account details could have been compromised. That ruined the entire experience for me. Otherwise, it was a good lunch for my colleagues and I. One more thing, AC is weak in the restaurant. Possibly due to it being an old structure.
